text:
At the foot of tall mountains, in a small village, lived a water carrier named Anvar. The village had no well, so every morning Anvar walked to a spring at the foot of the mountains and brought water back for everyone.

He had two large clay pots. He hung them on the two ends of a long wooden pole and carried them across his shoulders. One pot was perfect: smooth and whole. The other was just as useful, but it had a thin crack along its side.

The road from the spring to the village was long, half an hour’s walk. The perfect pot, filled at the spring, delivered its water to the house full, without losing a single drop. But the cracked pot leaked slowly along the way and arrived only half full.

Two years passed like this. Every day, Anvar brought one full pot and one half-full pot to the village.

The perfect pot was proud of itself. “I am flawless,” it would say. “I do my job completely.” But the cracked pot suffered from shame every day. “I only do half of my job,” it thought. “I’m useless. Anvar works so hard, and I spill water onto the road.”

One morning, at the spring, the cracked pot couldn’t hold back any longer and spoke to Anvar.

“I want to apologize,” it said in a trembling voice. “I am so ashamed.”

Anvar was surprised. “Why? What have you done?”

“For two years, I’ve delivered only half my water,” said the pot. “Because of the crack in my side, water leaks out along the way. You walk such a long distance, you work so hard, and I waste half your effort. I’m ashamed that I’m not like the other pot.”

Anvar was quiet for a moment. Then he smiled warmly and said, “On the way back today, look at the path. Look at both sides of the road.”

They set off. The cracked pot looked at the roadside and couldn’t believe its eyes. On one side of the path bloomed countless beautiful flowers: red tulips, yellow marigolds, blue hyacinths. The foot of the mountain looked as if it were covered with a colorful carpet.

“Do you see?” said Anvar. “The flowers grow only on your side. On the side where the perfect pot hangs, there isn’t a single flower.”

The pot said nothing.

“I noticed your crack on the very first day,” Anvar continued. “Two years ago, on my way back from the spring, I scattered flower seeds along your side of the road. And every day, as you came back from the spring, you watered them without knowing it. For two years now, I’ve picked these flowers to decorate my home, to sell at the market, to give to my neighbors. If you hadn’t been cracked, this beauty would never have existed.”

The cracked pot fell silent. Something inside it changed. What it had considered its greatest flaw for two years had turned out to be its greatest gift.

From that day on, the pot lived differently. It no longer felt ashamed of its crack, and it gazed tenderly at the flowers along the road. Every time a new flower bloomed, it felt a quiet joy.

And Anvar knew one thing: nothing is perfect, but everything has its own place and its own worth.

Moral: We all have our cracks: flaws, weaknesses, mistakes. Don’t rush to hide them or feel ashamed of them. Sometimes those very flaws bring beauty into other people’s lives. You may be growing flowers you can’t even see.

tr.title: Yorilgan ko’za
paragraphs: Baland tog’lar etagida, kichik bir qishloqda Anvar ismli suvchi yashar ekan. Qishloqda quduq yo’q ekan, shuning uchun har kuni ertalab Anvar tog’ etagidagi buloqqa borib, qishloq uchun suv olib kelar ekan.

Uning ikkita katta sopol ko’zasi bor ekan. Ularni uzun yog’och tayoqning ikki uchiga osib, yelkasida ko’tarib yurar ekan. Ko’zalarning biri mukammal, silliq va butun ekan. Ikkinchisi esa yaroqli bo’lsa ham, yon tomonida ingichka bir yorig’i bor ekan.

Buloqdan qishloqqacha yo’l uzun, yarim soatlik ekan. Butun ko’za buloqdan to’la suv olib, uyga qadar bir tomchi ham to’kmay yetib borar ekan. Yorilgan ko’za esa yo’lda sekin-sekin suv oqizib, manzilga yetganda yarmigacha bo’sh qolar ekan.
Shunday qilib, ikki yil o’tibdi. Har kuni Anvar qishloqqa bir ko’za to’la va bir ko’za yarim suv olib kelibdi.

Butun ko’za o’zi bilan faxrlanar ekan. «Men mukammalman», derkan u. «Men o’z vazifamni to’liq bajaraman.» Yorilgan ko’za esa har kuni xijolat chekib yashar ekan. «Men o’z vazifamning faqat yarmini bajaraman», deb o’ylar ekan. «Men yaroqsizman. Anvar menga qancha mehnat qiladi, men esa suvni yo’lga to’kib yuboraman.»
Bir kuni ertalab, buloq bo’yida, yorilgan ko’za chiday olmay Anvarga gapiribdi.
«Men sendan uzr so’rayman», debdi u titroq ovozda. «Men juda xijolatdaman.»
Anvar ajablanib so’rabdi: «Nima uchun? Nima qildim deysan?»

«Ikki yildan beri men suvning faqat yarmini yetkazib kelaman», debdi ko’za. «Yon tomonimdagi yoriq tufayli yo’lda suv oqib ketadi. Sen shuncha yo’l bosasan, shuncha mehnat qilasan, men esa mehnatingning yarmini bekor qilaman. Boshqa ko’zalar kabi bo’lolmaganimdan uyalaman.»
Anvar bir oz jim turibdi. Keyin mehr bilan jilmayib debdi: «Bugun qaytayotganda yo’lga e’tibor ber. Yo’lning ikki yog’iga qarab ko’r.»

Ular yo’lga tushibdi. Yorilgan ko’za yo’l bo’yiga qaragan ekan va ko’zlariga ishonmabdi. Yo’lning bir tomonida son-sanoqsiz chiroyli gullar ochilib yotgan ekan: qizil lolalar, sariq jambil, ko’k sunbullar. Tog’ etagi go’yo rangli gilam bilan qoplangandek ekan.
«Ko’ryapsanmi?» debdi Anvar. «Gullar faqat sening tomoningda o’sgan. Butun ko’zaning tomonida bitta ham gul yo’q.»

«Men sening yorig’ingni birinchi kunning o’zidayoq payqaganman», deb davom etibdi Anvar. «Ikki yil oldin, buloqdan qaytayotganda, yo’lning sening tomoningga gul urug’larini sepib chiqdim. Har kuni sen buloqdan qaytayotganda, bilmagan holda ularni sug’orib kelding. Ikki yildan beri men bu gullarni terib, uyimni bezayman, bozorda sotaman, qo’shnilarga sovg’a qilaman. Agar sen shunday yorilgan bo’lmaganingda, bu go’zallik hech qachon bo’lmasdi.»
Yorilgan ko’za jim qolibdi. Uning ichida nimadir o’zgaribdi. Ikki yil davomida u o’zining eng katta kamchiligi deb hisoblagan narsa aslida eng katta sovg’a bo’lib chiqqan ekan.
Shu kundan keyin ko’za boshqacha yashay boshlabdi. U endi yorig’idan uyalmay, yo’l bo’yidagi gullarga mehr bilan qarab ketar ekan. Har gal gul ochilsa, ichida ohista quvonch sezar ekan.
Anvar esa bir narsani bilar ekan: hech bir narsa mukammal emas, lekin har bir narsaning o’z o’rni va o’z qadri bor.

Qissadan hissa: Hammamizning o’z yoriqlarimiz bor: kamchiliklar, zaifliklar, xatolar. Ularni yashirishga, ulardan uyalishga shoshilma. Ba’zan aynan shu kamchiliklaring boshqalar hayotiga go’zallik olib keladi. Sen o’zing ko’rmaydigan gullarni o’stirib yurgan bo’lishing mumkin.

quiz.q: Anvar carried two clay pots on a wooden pole.
The perfect pot leaked water along the way.
Why did flowers grow on one side of the path?
o: The cracked pot watered the seeds Anvar planted
It rained more on that side

quiz.q: How long did Anvar carry water like this?
The cracked pot arrived only half ___.
